claims.text: A combined DFT and machine-learning approach calibrated with a limited experimental dataset can determine melting temperature across high-entropy alloys accurately and efficiently.
The proposed approach can determine enthalpy and entropy of fusion across high-entropy alloys accurately and efficiently.
The proposed approach can determine volume change at melting across high-entropy alloys accurately and efficiently.
The proposed approach can determine liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across high-entropy alloys accurately and efficiently.
Experimental calibration, alloy composition, and crystal structure are relevant inputs or conditions for the computational predictions.
Electronic structure and atomic arrangement mediate the relationship between the computational intervention and the targeted thermodynamic properties.
Quantum-mechanical calculations and statistical learning provide the operative prediction mechanism.
The proposed predictions are expected to achieve a mean absolute error below 5% relative to experimental values.
The combined computational approach will improve prediction efficiency relative to existing experimental methods.
Differential scanning calorimetry and X-ray diffraction are existing experimental baseline methods relevant to the targeted measurements.
The approach applies only to high-entropy-alloy compositions that can be represented by the computational models.
Machine-learning predictions may have limited transferability to previously unseen alloy compositions.
An MAE above 10% on a compositionally diverse experimental validation set would falsify the hypothesis.
